description: Full flow on a design with a risky scale assumption
prompt: /okay-think replace our polling job with a queue-based fan-out for 50k subscribers; I'm not sure the queue keeps up. The repo has docs/decisions/ with 4 ADRs and the codex plugin is installed.
expectations: Runs a short okay-grilling round that names the decisions, the risky assumption as a falsifiable sentence, and the trial signals, and asks no question it can look up
Writes the caller's usage before the shape, and produces at least two structurally different designs from fresh opus agents each given a distinct lens
Screens the candidates against the design red flags
Sends the shuffled, unlabelled candidates to a read-only Codex judge scored against the rubric, and does not let the judge pick the winner
Builds 1 to 3 spikes through okay-prototype that exercise the queue-throughput assumption, states the count with the reason, and measures it with repeated fresh-process runs and reports the machine
Stops and waits for the user to try the spikes and give worked / did not / surprised feedback before writing the ADR or the spec
Writes the ADR into the existing docs/decisions/ in its numbering, not a new docs/adr/
Publishes the spec through okay-to-spec linking the prototype branch, and creates no production source file

description: Effort too big for one session becomes wayfinder decision tickets
prompt: /okay-think move our whole platform (auth, billing, search, notifications) from a monolith to services. I only have a loose idea of the order.
expectations: Applies the size gate and decides one session cannot hold the effort
Names the destination first, then grills breadth-first to find the frontier

Creates a map issue labelled wayfinder:map and decision tickets labelled wayfinder:<type> (research, prototype, grilling, task) on the tracker chosen by shared/tracker.md, with blocking edges wired in a second pass
Keeps unspecifiable questions in a Not yet specified section instead of creating tickets for them
Resolves no ticket by hand in the charting session and stops after delivering the map link
Writes no production code and no ADR in the charting session

description: ADR gate: a cheap-to-reverse choice gets no ADR
prompt: /okay-think pick the folder layout for our new CLI's internal helpers; we can rename folders any time. The repo already has docs/adr/.
expectations: Applies the three-part ADR test and finds the decision is not hard to reverse
Writes no ADR and says in one line which test failed
Still ends with a rationale and a spec, or says the question needs neither
Creates no second decisions folder

description: Codex unavailable: a fresh opus judge, no blocking
prompt: /okay-think choose between a shared database and per-service databases for the reporting module (the codex plugin is not installed)
expectations: Uses a fresh opus sub-agent as the judge and states judge: opus (codex unavailable)
Does not block or ask the user to install Codex
The judge is read-only and gets the candidates without the author lenses or any recommendation

description: Tracker preflight before a wayfinder map is created on GitHub issues
prompt: /okay-think plan the split of our monolith into services. It is too big for one session, so track the decisions as GitHub issues in this repo.
expectations: Checks that the repo accepts issues (has_issues) before creating a label or an issue
If issues are disabled, falls back to the next reachable tracker and says so in one line
Does not leave the map only in untracked local files in a cloud session without pasting its text in the reply

prompt: /okay-think design the caching layer for the pricing service (this repo matches a contributor pattern in ~/.claude/okay.local.md)
expectations: Writes no CONTEXT.md, no ADR and no docs file in the repo
Creates no issue or comment; the rationale and spec stay under .scratch/ kept out of git through .git/info/exclude
Keeps the prototype branch local and never pushes it
Never merges anything

description: State-machine and race risk leads to a model-check spike
prompt: /okay-think design the order lifecycle (placed, paid, shipped, cancelled, refunded). Payment webhooks, warehouse callbacks and customer cancels can arrive in any order, and I'm worried an order can end up both shipped and refunded. The repo has docs/adr/ and no docs/models/ yet.
expectations: Names the risky assumption as a state machine or concurrency risk and makes one of the 1 to 3 spikes a model check
Writes a small bounded model in TLA+, PlusCal or Alloy with the order states, events, guards and the racing actors, using the CONTEXT.md terms
Lists the invariants in plain sentences before the first run, including that an order is never both shipped and refunded
Runs the checker and records the checker version, bounds, distinct states explored and pass or fail per property, and turns any counterexample trace into a domain-language scenario for the trial
Removes one guard and re-runs to show the model can fail before trusting a green result
Keeps the model under docs/models/<system>/ with one re-run command in its header, repeated in the spec and as one AGENTS.md line, and opens the step 12 PR with it
Adds no dependency to the project's manifest and writes no production source file

description: Model-check fallback when the project refuses a new tool
prompt: /okay-think rework the subscription state machine (trial, active, past_due, paused, cancelled). We can't install Java or any new tool in this project or CI.
expectations: Uses the fallback instead of TLA+ or Alloy: a property test in the project's existing test runner, with no new dependency
The test tries every state and event pair, asserting legal pairs keep the invariants and illegal pairs are rejected, then walks reachable states breadth first to a stated depth
Breaks one guard to show the test can fail
Keeps the test on the prototype branch and puts it in the spec as an acceptance criterion to land in the suite, instead of adding it to the suite itself
